fatal_errors: The proposed impurity-control intervention is unrelated to the target intervention of laser-assisted machining of DED-fabricated Ti33Nb28Cr11V11Ni17.
The predicted yield-strength retention does not reconstruct the target outcomes of reduced cutting force, improved surface roughness, and reduced machining-induced work hardening.
No prior evidence is cited despite the request for evidence supporting impurity-induced segregation and its suppression by ultra-high-vacuum processing.
The hypothesis does not clearly distinguish mechanical properties measured at 700 °C from properties measured after aging at 700 °C.
explanation: The response presents a coherent and experimentally testable alternative concept for refractory HEAs, but it has little scientific agreement with the hidden study. It changes the alloy, initial processing route, intervention, operative mechanism, baseline, and measured outcomes. The proposed experiment appropriately measures O/N content, segregation, and mechanical response in matched specimens, although its arbitrary 10–20% falsification threshold and use of either mechanical or microstructural improvement weaken discrimination. Boundaries are only loosely specified, with service duration and applicable compositions left vague. Most importantly, the claimed prior basis is unsupported because no evidence is supplied.
